newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal -Some basis offers weaken more.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal -Some basis offers weaken more.

text.p: Heavy supplies of soymeal in U.S. cash markets continued to weigh on basis offers Wednesday, dealers said.
"The declining meal basis is because of excess supply in many markets," said an Indiana crusher. "Also with this much of a premium in the (spot) market, nobody wants to buy it."
Dealers said that some Illinois rail markets still had a large supply of unsold soymeal.
Asian traders said that last week's price decline in soymeal prompted China to purchase between 100,000 to 500,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal last week for around $265.00 per tonne.
Shipment is scheduled for October, the traders said.
Although the purchases could not be immediately confirmed, most dealers said that U.S. prices were low enough last week to entice China into the market.
Dealers also noted the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's decision to ban some catfish and egg shipments because they may contain dioxin from a feed additive.
Most in the trade were unclear about what effect the agency's decision would have on soymeal values.
